simple.meaning: גָּרַד (gârad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to abrade.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Job, beginning at Job 2:8. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּרַד (H1623) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּרַד (gârad) / H1623 is traced through Job 2:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1623. garad [ גָּרַד ] verb scrape, scratch (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic גְּרַד , & Phoenician מגרדם flesh-scrapers CIS 338. 4 ; compare also Arabic peel or strip off bark, shave hair from a hide etc.) — Hithpa`el Infinitive לְהִתְגָּרֵד scrape one's self Job 2:8 .

occurrences.englishText: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
